topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing, lecturer background, and key learning outcomes for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Conceptual Frameworks and Evidence for Cancer Causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the relative contributions of intrinsic biological bad luck, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures to cancer development through conceptual models and epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections promote malignancy, highlighted by the epidemiology and molecular mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Direct and Metabolically Activated Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, physical, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing and cause direct DNA adducts or damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promoters, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how non-mutagenic promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and specific host developmental stages facilitate the outgrowth of mutated cells.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic mutational signature analyses, epidemiological biobanks, in vivo animal studies, and in vitro tests used to identify and validate carcinogens.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of environmental cancer drivers and the everyday balance between carcinogen risks and practical benefits.
